subject: math
title: Grade 4 Decimals to Hundredths
seo_title: Grade 4 Decimals to Hundredths Worksheets: Free Math Practice with Answer Key (BC Curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 math worksheets on decimals to hundredths for the BC curriculum: tenths and 3/10 = 0.3, hundred grids, place value, comparing and ordering decimals, and money and measurement like $4.35 and 0.75 m. 100 questions with an answer key, good FSA numeracy practice.
key_big: Tenths are the first place after the decimal point; hundredths are the second. 3/10 = 0.3 and 27/100 = 0.27.
key_sub: Compare by place value, not by length: 0.5 = 0.50 > 0.45. 0.3 is 3/10, not 3/100, and 7/100 is 0.07, not 0.7.
body_html:
Tenths

Split 1 whole into 10 equal parts. Each part is one tenth: 110 = 0.1. Tenths go in the first place after the decimal point.

Hundredths

Split 1 whole into 100 equal parts. Each part is one hundredth: 1100 = 0.01. Hundredths go in the second place after the decimal point. 10 hundredths make 1 tenth.

Place value

Each digit has a place: ones, then the decimal point, then tenths and hundredths. Use a 0 to hold an empty place: 7100 = 0.07.

Example 1

Write 8100 as a decimal.

8 hundredths. There are 0 tenths, so put a 0 in the tenths place.

Answer: 0.08

Comparing decimals

Compare the ones first, then the tenths, then the hundredths. It helps to give both numbers the same number of places: 0.5 = 0.50.

Example 2

Order 0.6, 0.35 and 0.4 from smallest to greatest.

Compare the tenths: 3, 4 and 6.

Answer: 0.35, 0.4, 0.6

Money and measurement

Cents are hundredths of a dollar: $4.35 = 4 dollars and 35 cents = 435¢. Centimetres are hundredths of a metre: 0.75 m = 75 cm and 1.25 m = 1 m 25 cm.

Example 3

Which costs more: $3.50 or $3.05?

Compare the tenths: 5 tenths (50¢) and 0 tenths (5¢).

Answer: $3.50

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
0.45 > 0.5 because 45 > 5Use the same places: 0.45 < 0.50
Writing 7 tenths as 0.07Tenths use the first place: 0.7
Reading 0.3 as 31000.3 is 3 tenths: 310
Writing 7100 as 0.7Hundredths need two places: 0.07
Counting 0.28, 0.29, 0.21010 hundredths make 1 tenth: 0.29, 0.30

faq.q: What do Grade 4 students learn about decimals in BC?
faq.a: The BC Grade 4 math curriculum includes decimals to hundredths. Students show tenths and hundredths with strips and hundred grids, connect them to fractions like 3/10 = 0.3 and 27/100 = 0.27, and compare decimals in money and measurement.

faq.q: How do you explain tenths and hundredths to a child?
faq.a: Use a strip split into 10 equal parts for tenths and a hundred grid for hundredths. Each part of the strip is 0.1 and each small square is 0.01, so 27 shaded squares show 0.27.
The 5 in 0.5 means 5 tenths, which is 50 hundredths. 0.45 is only 45 hundredths, so 0.5 is bigger even though it has fewer digits.

faq.q: Do these decimal worksheets help with the Grade 4 FSA?
faq.a: Yes. The Grade 4 FSA includes numeracy, where students use number sense to solve problems. Reading prices, lengths and amounts written as decimals, as in these worksheets, is good practice for it.

items.q: The strip is 1 whole. What decimal is shaded?
items.e: The strip is 1 whole split into 10 equal parts, so each part is 1 tenth. 3 parts are shaded: 310 = 0.3. Tenths go in the first place after the decimal point (not 0.03).

items.q: The strip is 1 whole. What decimal is shaded?
items.e: The strip is 1 whole split into 10 equal parts, so each part is 1 tenth. 7 parts are shaded: 710 = 0.7. Tenths go in the first place after the decimal point (not 0.07). 0.3 is the part that is not shaded.

items.q: The strip is 1 whole. What decimal is shaded?
items.e: The strip is 1 whole split into 10 equal parts, so each part is 1 tenth. 5 parts are shaded: 510 = 0.5. Tenths go in the first place after the decimal point (not 0.05).

items.q: 1 whole is split into 10 equal parts. What decimal is each part?
items.e: Each part is 110 of the whole, one tenth: 0.1. 0.01 is one hundredth.

items.q: How many tenths make 1 whole?
items.e: 1 whole split into 10 equal parts: 1010 = 1. So 10 tenths make 1 whole.

items.q: Write 310 as a decimal.
items.e: 310 is 3 tenths. Tenths go in the first place after the decimal point: 0.3. 0.03 would be 3 hundredths.

items.q: Write 910 as a decimal.
items.e: 910 is 9 tenths. Tenths go in the first place after the decimal point: 0.9. 0.09 would be 9 hundredths.

items.q: Write 610 as a decimal.
items.e: 610 is 6 tenths. Tenths go in the first place after the decimal point: 0.6. 0.06 would be 6 hundredths.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 0.3?
items.e: 0.3 has one digit after the point, so it means tenths: 3 tenths = 310. It is not 3100 (that is 0.03) and not 13 (3 out of 10 parts, not 1 out of 3).

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 0.8?
items.e: One digit after the point means tenths: 0.8 = 8 tenths = 810. 8100 is 0.08.

items.q: All four strips are the same size. Which strip shows 0.6?
items.e: 0.6 is 6 tenths, so the strip must have 10 equal parts with 6 shaded: strip B. A shows 0.4. C shows 16, not 0.6. D has 6 shaded, but it has 12 parts, so it shows 612, which is one half (0.5).

items.q: What decimal is at the red dot?
items.e: The line from 0 to 1 has 10 equal spaces, so each space is 1 tenth (0.1). The dot is 3 spaces after 0: 0.3.

items.q: What decimal is at the red dot?
items.e: Each of the 10 spaces is 0.1. The dot is 8 spaces after 0: 0.8. (0.2 counts the 2 spaces back from 1, the wrong end.)

items.q: Each strip is 1 whole. What decimal is shaded?
items.e: One whole strip is shaded (1) and 4 tenths of the second strip: 1 and 410 = 1.4. 0.14 would be only 14 hundredths.

items.q: Each strip is 1 whole. What decimal is shaded?
items.e: Two whole strips are shaded (2) and 3 tenths of the third strip: 2 and 310 = 2.3. 2.03 would be 2 and 3 hundredths.

items.q: Write 2 710 as a decimal.
items.e: 2 wholes, then the decimal point, then 7 tenths in the first place: 2.7. 2.07 would be 7 hundredths.

items.q: How many tenths are there in 3.2?
items.e: 1 whole = 10 tenths, so 3 wholes = 30 tenths. 30 + 2 = 32 tenths. (2 is only the digit in the tenths place.)

items.q:
Count on in tenths. What comes next?
0.7, 0.8, 0.9, ?
items.e: 0.9 + 0.1: 9 tenths and 1 more make 10 tenths, which is 1 whole. So the next number is 1 (or 1.0). 0.10 is only 1 tenth.

items.q: Start at 0.8 on a number line. Jump on 3 tenths. Where do you land?
items.e: 0.9, 1.0, 1.1. 10 tenths make 1 whole, so 0.8 + 0.3 = 1.1. 0.83 jumps 3 hundredths, and 0.5 jumps back.

items.q: Kai’s chocolate bar has 10 equal pieces. He eats 7 pieces. What decimal of the bar is left?
items.e: 10 − 7 = 3 pieces are left. Each piece is 1 tenth, so 310 of the bar is left: 0.3. 0.7 is the part he ate.

items.q: The whole grid is 1. What decimal is shaded?
items.e: Each full column is 1 tenth. 4 full columns are shaded: 4 tenths = 410 = 0.4 (or 0.40). 0.04 would be only 4 small squares.

items.q: The whole grid is 1. What decimal is shaded?
items.e: Each full column is 1 tenth and each small square is 1 hundredth. 2 full columns and 7 squares are shaded: 2 tenths and 7 hundredths = 27100 = 0.27.

items.q: The whole grid is 1. What decimal is shaded?
items.e: Each small square is 1 hundredth. 6 squares are shaded and there is no full column, so there are 0 tenths. 6 hundredths = 6100 = 0.06. Write a 0 in the tenths place.

items.q: The whole grid is 1. What decimal is shaded?
items.e: Each full column is 1 tenth and each small square is 1 hundredth. 5 full columns and 8 squares are shaded: 5 tenths and 8 hundredths = 58100 = 0.58.

items.q: The whole grid is 1. What decimal is shaded?
items.e: Each full column is 1 tenth and each small square is 1 hundredth. 6 full columns and 4 squares are shaded: 6 tenths and 4 hundredths = 64100 = 0.64. 0.36 is the part that is not shaded.

items.q: The whole grid is 1. What decimal is shaded?
items.e: Each full column is 1 tenth and each small square is 1 hundredth. 9 full columns and 1 square are shaded: 9 tenths and 1 hundredth = 91100 = 0.91.

items.q: The whole grid is 1. What decimal is shaded?
items.e: Each small square is 1 hundredth. 3 squares are shaded and there is no full column, so there are 0 tenths. 3 hundredths = 3100 = 0.03. Write a 0 in the tenths place. 0.97 is the part that is not shaded.

items.q: 1 whole is split into 100 equal parts. What decimal is each part?
items.e: Each part is 1100 of the whole, one hundredth: 0.01. 0.1 is one tenth: 1 whole split into 10 parts.

items.q: How many hundredths make 1 tenth?
items.e: On a hundred grid, 1 column is 1 tenth and it has 10 small squares. So 10 hundredths = 1 tenth.

items.q: Write 27100 as a decimal.
items.e: 27100 is 27 hundredths: 2 tenths and 7 hundredths. The tenths digit is 2 and the hundredths digit is 7: 0.27.

items.q: Write 8100 as a decimal.
items.e: 8100 is 8 hundredths. Hundredths need two places after the point, so write a 0 in the tenths place: 0.08. (0.8 would be 8 tenths.)

items.q: Write 50100 as a decimal.
items.e: 50100 is 50 hundredths, which is the same as 5 tenths: 0.5 (or 0.50). 0.05 would be only 5 hundredths.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 0.07?
items.e: 0.07 has two digits after the point, so it means hundredths. The tenths digit is 0: 0.07 = 7 hundredths = 7100. (710 is 0.7.)

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 0.45?
items.e: Two digits after the point means hundredths: 0.45 = 45 hundredths = 45100.

items.q: 0.6 is the same as how many hundredths?
items.e: 0.6 = 6 tenths. Each tenth is 10 hundredths, so 6 tenths = 60 hundredths = 60100. 6100 is only 0.06.

items.q: Which hundred grid shows 0.3?
items.e: 0.3 is 3 tenths, which is 3 full columns (30 small squares): grid C. A shows 0.03, B shows 0.13 and D shows 0.7.

items.q: Which decimal is 6 tenths and 2 hundredths?
items.e: Tenths go in the first place after the point and hundredths in the second: 0.62.

items.q:
Count on in hundredths. What comes next?
0.27, 0.28, 0.29, ?
items.e: 0.29 + 0.01: 9 hundredths and 1 more make 10 hundredths, which is 1 more tenth. So 2 tenths become 3 tenths: 0.30 (the same as 0.3). There is no such step as 0.210.

items.q: The whole grid is 1. What decimal is not shaded?
items.e: 35 of the 100 squares are shaded, so 100 − 35 = 65 squares are not shaded: 0.65. 0.35 is the shaded part. Check: 0.35 + 0.65 = 1 (but 0.35 + 0.75 = 1.1, too much).

items.q: Simran colours 45 squares of a hundred grid red and 30 squares blue. What decimal of the grid is coloured?
items.e: 45 + 30 = 75 squares are coloured. That is 75 hundredths: 75100 = 0.75. 0.25 is the part that is left white.

sets.title: Place value: ones, tenths and hundredths

items.q: What is the value of the red digit in 4.37?
items.e: The red 3 is in the first place after the decimal point, in the tenths column. Its value is 3 tenths = 0.3.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit in 2.58?
items.e: The red 8 is in the second place after the decimal point, in the hundredths column. Its value is 8 hundredths = 0.08.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit in 6.09?
items.e: The red 9 is in the second place after the decimal point, in the hundredths column. Its value is 9 hundredths = 0.09. The 0 holds the tenths place.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit in 15.6?
items.e: The red 5 is just before the decimal point, in the ones column. Its value is 5 ones.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 7 in 3.72?
items.e: In 3.72 the 7 is in the first place after the point, the tenths place. It is worth 0.7.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 4 in 8.14?
items.e: In 8.14 the 4 is in the second place after the point, the hundredths place. It is worth 0.04.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 6 in 6.25?
items.e: In 6.25 the 6 is before the decimal point, in the ones place. It is worth 6.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 9 in 12.9?
items.e: In 12.9 the 9 is in the first place after the point, the tenths place. It is worth 0.9.

items.q: In 19.25, which digit is in the tenths place?
items.e: 19.25: tens 1, ones 9, then the point, tenths 2, hundredths 5. The tenths digit is 2.

items.q: In 47.36, which digit is in the hundredths place?
items.e: 47.36: tens 4, ones 7, then the point, tenths 3, hundredths 6. The hundredths digit is 6.

items.q: In 30.48, which digit is in the ones place?
items.e: 30.48: tens 3, ones 0, then the point, tenths 4, hundredths 8. The ones digit is 0.
4 ones, 6 tenths and 3 hundredths: 4 . 6 3 = 4.63.
There are no tenths, so write a 0 in the tenths place: 2 . 0 8 = 2.08. 2.8 would be 2 ones and 8 tenths.

items.q: Which shows 5.29 in expanded form?
items.e: 5 ones, 2 tenths and 9 hundredths: 5 + 0.2 + 0.09.

items.q: Which decimal is 3 tens, 1 one and 6 hundredths?
items.e: 3 tens and 1 one make 31. There are 0 tenths, so write a 0 before the 6 hundredths: 31.06.

items.q: How many hundredths are there in 0.9?
items.e: 1 tenth = 10 hundredths, so 9 tenths = 90 hundredths. 0.9 = 0.90.

items.q: How many hundredths are there in 0.35?
items.e: 0.35 = 3 tenths and 5 hundredths. 3 tenths = 30 hundredths, and 30 + 5 = 35 hundredths. So 0.35 = 35100.

items.q: How many tenths are there in 2.4?
items.e: 1 whole = 10 tenths, so 2 wholes = 20 tenths. 20 + 4 = 24 tenths. (4 is only the digit in the tenths place.)

items.q: 0.73 = 7 tenths and ? hundredths
items.e: 0.73 = 0.7 + 0.03. So 0.73 = 7 tenths and 3 hundredths.

items.q: 0.73 = 6 tenths and ? hundredths
items.e: Take 1 of the 7 tenths and rename it as 10 hundredths: 10 + 3 = 13. So 0.73 = 6 tenths and 13 hundredths (0.6 + 0.13 = 0.73).

items.q: Compare the decimals.
items.e: Both have 0 ones. Compare the tenths: 3 tenths < 7 tenths. So 0.3 < 0.7.

items.q: Compare the decimals.
items.e: Compare the ones first: 1.4 has 1 one and 0.9 has 0 ones. So 1.4 > 0.9, even though 9 > 4.

items.q: Compare the decimals.
items.e: Compare the tenths first: 6 tenths > 2 tenths. So 0.62 > 0.26.

items.q: Compare the decimals.
items.e: 0.8 = 0.80. Compare the tenths: 0.08 has 0 tenths and 0.80 has 8 tenths. So 0.08 < 0.8.

items.q: Which decimal is the greatest?
items.e: All have 0 ones. Compare the tenths: 6, 4, 0 and 5. 0.6 has the most tenths, so it is the greatest, even though 0.48 has more digits.

items.q: Which decimal is the smallest?
items.e: Compare the tenths: 0.25 has 2 tenths, the others have 3 or 4. So 0.25 is the smallest.

items.q: Which decimal is the smallest?
items.e: 0.07 has 0 tenths. All the others have at least 1 tenth. So 0.07 is the smallest.

items.q: Which decimal is equal to 0.4?
items.e: 0.4 = 4 tenths = 40 hundredths = 0.40. A 0 at the end does not change the value. 0.04 is only 4 hundredths.

items.q: Compare the decimals.
items.e: Write 0.5 as 0.50 so both have hundredths. 50 hundredths > 45 hundredths, so 0.5 > 0.45. Do not compare 5 with 45: the 5 in 0.5 is 5 tenths.

items.q: Compare the decimals.
items.e: Compare the tenths first: 3 tenths < 4 tenths. So 0.39 < 0.4. (0.4 = 0.40, and 39 < 40.)

items.q: Compare the decimals.
items.e: Both have 2 ones. Compare the tenths: 2.07 has 0 tenths and 2.7 has 7 tenths. So 2.07 < 2.7.

items.q: Compare the decimals.
items.e: A 0 at the end of a decimal does not change its value: 5 tenths = 50 hundredths. So 3.5 = 3.50.

items.q: Which number is greater than 0.5?
items.e: 0.5 has 5 tenths. 0.61 has 6 tenths, so 0.61 > 0.5. 0.49 and 0.45 have only 4 tenths, and 0.05 has 0 tenths.

items.q: Which decimal is the greatest?
items.e: 0.95 and 0.99 have 0 ones, so they are less than 1. Compare 1.2 and 1.09: 2 tenths > 0 tenths. So 1.2 is the greatest.

items.q: Which number is between 0.4 and 0.5?
items.e: 0.4 = 0.40 and 0.5 = 0.50. 0.45 is 45 hundredths, which is between 40 and 50 hundredths.

items.q: Which statement is true?
items.e: 0.6 = 0.60, and 60 hundredths > 59 hundredths. So 0.6 > 0.59 is true.

items.q: Order from smallest to greatest: 0.6, 0.35, 0.4
items.e: Compare the tenths: 0.35 has 3, 0.4 has 4 and 0.6 has 6. So the order is 0.35, 0.4, 0.6. 0.35 is not the biggest just because 35 is a bigger number than 4 or 6.

items.q: Order from smallest to greatest: 1.2, 0.8, 1.05
items.e: 0.8 has 0 ones, so it is the smallest. 1.05 has 0 tenths and 1.2 has 2 tenths, so 1.05 < 1.2. Order: 0.8, 1.05, 1.2.

items.q: Order from greatest to smallest: 0.7, 0.75, 0.57
items.e: Write them with hundredths: 0.70, 0.75, 0.57. Greatest to smallest: 75, 70, 57 hundredths, so 0.75, 0.7, 0.57. Careful: the question asks for greatest first.

items.q: Order from smallest to greatest: 2.3, 2.03, 2.33
items.e: All have 2 ones. Write them with hundredths: 2.30, 2.03, 2.33. 3 < 30 < 33 hundredths, so 2.03, 2.3, 2.33.

items.q: How many cents is $4.35?
A granola bar costs 75¢. How do you write 75¢ in dollars?
items.e: There are 100¢ in $1, so 75¢ = 75100 of a dollar = $0.75. ($7.50 is 750¢.)

items.q: Which amount is the same as 50¢?
items.e: 50¢ = 50 hundredths of a dollar = $0.50 (half a dollar). $0.05 is only 5¢, one nickel.

items.q: In $6.80, what is the digit 8 worth?
items.e: The 8 is in the tenths place: 8 tenths of a dollar. 810 of $1 = 80¢.

items.q: Which price tag shows 12 dollars and 5 cents?
items.e: Cents are hundredths of a dollar. 5¢ = 5 hundredths, so write a 0 in the tenths place: $12.05. $12.50 is 12 dollars and 50 cents.

items.q: Liam has a toonie, 2 dimes and a nickel. How much money is that?
items.e: A toonie is $2. 2 dimes = 20¢ and a nickel = 5¢, so 20¢ + 5¢ = 25¢. $2 + 25¢ = $2.25. ($27 adds 2 + 10 + 10 + 5, but the toonie is 200¢.)

items.q: Ava has a loonie and 3 quarters. How much money is that?
items.e: A loonie is $1. 3 quarters = 25¢ + 25¢ + 25¢ = 75¢. $1 + 75¢ = $1.75. ($4 just counts the coins, and $1.03 counts each quarter as 1¢.)

items.q: Which amount of money is the greatest?
items.e: 95¢ and $0.59 are less than $1. Compare $1.50 and $1.05: 5 tenths > 0 tenths. So $1.50 is the greatest.

items.q: At the school store, a muffin costs $2.50 and a cookie costs $2.05. Which costs more?
items.e: Both cost $2 and some cents. Compare the tenths: $2.50 has 5 tenths (50¢) and $2.05 has 0 tenths (5¢). So the muffin costs more.

items.q: Ethan has $2.40. His grandma gives him a loonie. How much money does he have now?
items.e: A loonie is $1. Add it to the dollars: $2 + $1 = $3. The cents stay the same: $3.40. ($2.41 adds 1¢, $2.50 adds 10¢, and $12.40 just writes the 1 in front.)

items.q: A ribbon is 1.25 m long. What does the 2 in 1.25 m mean?
items.e: The 2 is in the first place after the point, the tenths place. So it means 2 tenths of a metre (20 cm).

items.q: A pencil is 0.15 m long. 1 cm is 1100 of a metre. How long is the pencil in centimetres?
items.e: 0.15 m = 15 hundredths of a metre = 15100 m. Each hundredth of a metre is 1 cm, so the pencil is 15 cm.

items.q: Jasleen takes a 0.75 L water bottle on a hike. Which fraction of a litre is that?
items.e: 0.75 has two digits after the point, so it is hundredths: 75 hundredths = 75100 L (750 mL).

items.q: Jug A holds 2.5 L of water. Jug B holds 2.45 L. Which jug holds more?
items.e: Both hold 2 L and a bit more. 2.5 = 2.50. Compare 50 hundredths and 45 hundredths: Jug A holds more. 45 is bigger than 5, but the 5 in 2.5 means 5 tenths.

items.q: On track and field day, Chloe jumps 2.48 m and Arjun jumps 2.8 m in the long jump. Who jumps farther?
items.e: Both jumps are 2 whole metres. Compare the tenths: 2.8 has 8 tenths and 2.48 has 4 tenths. So Arjun jumps farther.

items.q: At a swim meet in Kamloops, Owen swims 25 m in 24.6 seconds. Mateo swims it in 24.06 seconds. Who is faster?
items.e: In a race, the shorter time is faster. 24.06 < 24.6 because 0 tenths < 6 tenths. So Mateo is faster.

items.q: Three students measure their height: Hana 1.3 m, Wei 1.28 m and Leah 1.35 m. Who is the tallest?
items.e: All are 1 m and a bit more. Write them with hundredths: 1.30, 1.28 and 1.35. 35 hundredths is the most, so Leah is the tallest.

items.q: A coho salmon from the Fraser River has a mass of 4.05 kg. Which is the same as 4.05 kg?
c: 4 kg and 5 hundredths of a kilogram
4 kg and 5 tenths of a kilogram
items.e: 4.05: 4 ones, 0 tenths and 5 hundredths. So it is 4 kg and 5 hundredths of a kilogram. 5 tenths would be 4.5 kg.

items.q: A 1 L carton of milk is full. Nadia pours out 0.3 L. How much milk is left?
items.e: 1 L = 10 tenths of a litre. 10 tenths − 3 tenths = 7 tenths = 0.7 L. 0.97 L would take away only 3 hundredths.

items.q: Zara pays for a hot chocolate at the skating rink with a $5 bill. It costs $2.70. How much change does she get?
